prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. ONE isolated Coriandrum sativum cilantro plant for image-to-3D in a Chinese Jiangnan miniature farm. Image 1 is STYLE ONLY: approved gongbi fine-line and light-colour painting, do not copy bok choy anatomy. Remaining images are real botanical anatomy references. Thin flat delicate leaves, slender connected GREEN petioles, fresh muted jade/sage greens with watercolor pigment mottling and CLEAR fine moss-green structural contour and vein lines which must survive 3D texturing. Natural matte surfaces, no inflated thick rubber leaves, no yellow vintage-paper wash, no neon green, no photographic noise. Plain neutral light-gray background, even neutral diffuse light, no cast shadow, no soil, pot, base disk, roots, text or extra objects. A single connected plant from short basal stem at soil line to all leaves, all joins visible/plausible, full silhouette framed with margin. Elevated three-quarter view 35 degrees down showing front/back volume, NOT a flat frontal fan or top-down herb diagram. Harvest-ready mature cilantro BEFORE bolting: compact airy tuft of SEVEN slender green petioles radiating in all directions from ONE basal crown. Outer leaves are ternately divided into a terminal rounded fan-shaped scalloped leaflet and two smaller lobed side leaflets, some younger inner leaves simpler with three broad rounded lobes. Distinctive rounded cilantro lobes with gentle fine teeth, NOT narrow fern leaves, not parsley spikes, not celery giant foliage. About 15-18 leaf blades total with deliberate spacing and clearly connected branching rachises, no excessive tiny noisy leaflets. Width similar to height, lower stem structure visible, mature bushy but airy crown with several front, side and back leaves and smaller central leaves. All leaf blades above short basal planting anchor. No flowers, seed umbels, long bolting stalk or bound harvested bundle.
